members.name: rbi_policy_reaction_v1
members.universe: BANK NIFTY index (via futures) and top 3 private bank stocks
members.thesis: RBI monetary policy announcements (6 per year, typically at 10:00 IST) create a predictable intraday pattern: (1) pre-announcement compression (09:15-10:00) where volatility drops and prices consolidate, (2) knee-jerk reaction (10:00-10:15) where BANK NIFTY moves 50-200 bps in the direction of the s
entry_long: PHASE 3 (10:15-10:45): banknifty_reaction < -50 bps (sold off on hawkish surprise) AND retracement_pct > 0.3 (already started bouncing)
OR PHASE 4 (10:45-12:00): banknifty_reaction > 0 (dovish surprise) AND close > VWAP AND gilt_yield_change < -3 bps (yields confirming dovishness)
entry_short: PHASE 3: banknifty_reaction > 50 bps (rallied on dovish surprise) AND retracement_pct > 0.3
OR PHASE 4: banknifty_reaction < 0 (hawkish surprise) AND close < VWAP AND gilt_yield_change > 3 bps
members.exit_target: Phase 3: 50% retracement of reaction move. Phase 4: 30 bps from entry
members.exit_stop: Phase 3: reaction_peak extends (new extreme). Phase 4: 15 bps from entry
filters: no VIX filter (VIX spike is part of the signal, not a filter)
only trade on RBI policy announcement days (6 per year)
BANK NIFTY volume > 1.5x normal on policy day (confirmed interest)
Phase 3 is contrarian (fade); Phase 4 follows confirmed trend
BANK NIFTY futures spread < 0.1% (spreads widen on policy day)
weaknesses: Only 6 trade days per year (RBI policy meetings) — the strategy cannot be a primary income source and contributes minimally to annual P&L.
The Phase 3/Phase 4 framework assumes a standard reaction pattern, but emergency meetings or coordinated global central bank actions create non-standard patterns.
Slippage on RBI policy days is significantly higher than normal — the 3 bps assumption is optimistic; actual slippage may be 5-10 bps during peak reaction.

members.name: budget_day_strategy_v1
members.thesis: Union Budget day (typically Feb 1) is the single highest-volatility scheduled event in Indian markets. The budget speech starts at 11:00 IST and runs for 90-120 minutes. The intraday pattern: (1) 09:15-11:00: pre-speech compression with low volume, (2) 11:00-12:30: sector-specific knee-jerk reaction
entry_long: sector_reaction_rank >= 8 (bottom 3 sectors — biggest losers during speech)
entry_short: sector_reaction_rank <= 2 (top 2 sectors — biggest winners during speech)
members.exit_target: 30-50% reversion of speech reaction (e.g., if lost 200 bps, target 60-100 bps recovery)
members.exit_stop: reaction extends by 50% beyond speech extreme (e.g., if lost 200 bps, stop at 300 bps loss)
filters: no VIX filter on budget day (VIX will be elevated by definition)
entry only in 12:30-13:30 window; exit by 15:15
sector stocks trading at > 2x normal volume (confirms interest)
fade extreme sector movers (contrarian by design)
bid-ask < 20 bps (wider tolerance on budget day)
weaknesses: Only 1 trade day per year. The strategy's contribution to annual P&L is minimal unless the edge per trade is very large (~50 bps) and size is scaled up.
Distinguishing structural budget changes (new tax, sector deregulation) from cyclical allocations (higher capex for one year) is qualitative and hard to automate.
Slippage on budget day is extreme — true slippage may be 10-20 bps, not 3 bps. The edge math assumes normal slippage which is unrealistic.
members.prior_art: Cutler, Poterba & Summers (1989) 'What Moves Stock Prices?' — event-driven returns. In India, Gupta & Kundu (2006) study budget day stock market reactions. Mohanty (2013) analyzes fiscal policy impact
